notes.summary: Calais Campbell, Marlon Humphrey, and Trey Hendrickson missed practice this week, severely limiting the Ravens' defensive front and secondary depth.
notes.speaker: Scott Bogman
notes.quote: Calais Campbell still not practicing, neither did Marlon Humphrey, Trey Hendrickson still down as well.

notes.summary: Falcons pass ruson Za'Darius Smith is questionable with a neck injury and has not practiced all week, potentially limiting Atlanta's pass rush.
notes.speaker: Scott Bogman
notes.quote: Zadarius Smith questionable for this game... neck injury... he has not practiced yet this week.

notes.summary: The Atlanta offense has transformed completely under Michael Penix Jr., scoring 70 combined points over his last two starts.
notes.speaker: Tera Roberts
notes.quote: This is just a team that looks so different with him at the helm.

notes.summary: Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle continues to aggressively prioritize Zay Flowers, giving him a 50% target share in the prior game.
notes.speaker: Tera Roberts
notes.quote: Declan Doyle has really placed Flowers as the focal point... had a 50% target share last week.

notes.summary: The Falcons defensive scheme under Kevin Stefanski is designed to contain mobile quarterbacks, having allowed the second fewest quarterback rushing yards the prior season.
notes.speaker: Scott Bogman
notes.quote: Stefanski last season 2025... they allowed the second fewest quarterback rushing yards... might just be a staple of Stefanski's defensive scheme.

notes.summary: The hosts note that Sean Payton has taken back playcalling responsibilities from offensive coordinator Davis Webb less than a month into the season, ending a very short-lived experiment.
notes.speaker: Derrik Klassen
notes.quote: Does Sean Payton taking back playcalling count as surprising news?

notes.topic: Mike Macdonald's schematic success against Kyle Shanahan
notes.summary: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald historically has had success scheming against Kyle Shanahan's offense, which presents a major schematic obstacle for the 49ers.
notes.speaker: Dave Helman
notes.quote: By the end of the year, you were like, 'Oh man, Mike Macdonald's got Kyle Shanahan's number, doesn't he?'

notes.topic: Physicality of the 49ers' interior offensive line
notes.summary: The 49ers' interior offensive line, featuring Colby and Puni, is playing with a much higher level of physicality than in previous years, which will be crucial with fullback Kyle Juszczyk sidelined.
notes.speaker: Dave Helman
notes.quote: I think you've just felt a different level of physicality from the interior for the Niners this year than we've become accustomed to.

notes.topic: Dominance of the Bills' defensive front
notes.summary: Derrik Klassen highlights the Bills' defensive line as playing out of their minds, collapsing pockets and setting edges at an elite level.
notes.speaker: Derrik Klassen
notes.quote: I think the front is playing out of their mind... Dion Walker, Ed Oliver... Landen Jackson...

notes.topic: Rams' pass protection breakdowns and Stafford's interceptions
notes.summary: Stafford has thrown 6 interceptions in 4 games primarily due to severe pass protection breakdowns in pure dropback situations, where he is unable to move and escape pressure.
notes.speaker: Derrik Klassen
notes.quote: Stafford struggle in pure pass protection... he's going to stand on his spot and if he's crowded he's going to throw it...

notes.summary: With Lane Johnson retiring and Cam Jurgens traded, the Eagles' line is severely depleted, leaving Jordan Mailata as the lone stabilizer from their elite championship-caliber core.
notes.speaker: Dave Helman
notes.quote: This is a team that was already on life support... Lane Johnson's gone, Jason Kelce is gone, Landon Dickerson is hurt...

notes.summary: Dave Helman emphasizes that the Vikings' offense has been historically unproductive for a 4-0 team, scoring only 86 points through four weeks, and desperately needs to show signs of life against the Saints.
notes.speaker: Dave Helman
notes.quote: I just need the Vikings to do anything on offense... score a touchdown.

notes.topic: Darnold middle of the field vulnerability
notes.summary: Warren Sharp noted Darnold relies heavily on passing between the numbers where he is highly efficient, but the 49ers defense funnels passers outside the numbers where Darnold is dead last in the league.
notes.speaker: Warren Sharp
notes.quote: This is going to be massive. The Niners funnel you outside. Darnold lives in the middle.

notes.topic: Bengals offensive splits without star WRs
notes.summary: Bengals likely using heavier, fewer-receiver personnel blocks the Dolphins' optimal defensive alignments, opening up highly efficient run paths for Chase Brown.
notes.speaker: Warren Sharp
notes.quote: The Bengals may not have three receivers to use. Chase Brown runs into the Dolphins' weak split.

notes.topic: Bears outside zone run identity vs Packers defense
notes.summary: Bears lean heavily on outside zone running, where the Packers defense is dead last in yards after contact allowed.
notes.speaker: Warren Sharp
notes.quote: Outside zone against a defense that cannot stop it.

notes.summary: Georgia heavily blitzed Ty Simpson in the SEC title game because he was terrible under pressure. Russell represents a substantial athletic upgrade capable of burning the blitz.
notes.speaker: Ryan McCrystal
notes.quote: They blitzed a season-high 51% of the time in that SEC title game... But Simpson's gone and they've got an upgrade at quarterback in Keelon Russell.

notes.topic: Arch Manning downfield passing accuracy concerns
notes.summary: Manning struggles with downfield accuracy (51% on-target rate beyond 10 yards) and taking sacks under pressure, which is a major concern facing Oklahoma's defensive unit.
notes.speaker: Ryan McCrystal
notes.quote: On throws 10 or more yards downfield, his on-target rate is 51%. That ranks 102nd in the country.

notes.topic: UCLA offensive scheme and run efficiency
notes.summary: UCLA's Bob Chesney utilizes James Madison transfers who are already highly comfortable with his offensive system, creating high yards-before-contact figures.
notes.speaker: Ryan McCrystal
notes.quote: Dean Kennedy designs the run game that creates a lot of open spaces for his team to run.

notes.topic: Tight end injuries dictating Rams personnel groupings
notes.summary: With key tight ends injured, the Rams are utilizing more 11 personnel, resulting in Kyren Williams absorbing a much larger share of team targets.
notes.speaker: Rich Hribar
notes.quote: The Rams have been forced to kind of abandon their heavy 13 personnel... pushing Kyren into a larger receiving role.

notes.topic: Carl Cheffers defensive pass interference calls
notes.summary: Carl Cheffers' crew aggressively penalizes defensive pass interference, a major vulnerability for both Detroit's and Arizona's defensive backfields.
notes.speaker: Joe Gibbs
notes.quote: Both the Cardinals and the Lions defenses rank as top 10 units surrendering defensive pass interference.

notes.summary: Brandon outlines Colts vs Steelers as a very poor spot for Indy coming back from London on short rest while Pittsburgh is resting at home on TNF.
notes.speaker: Brandon Anderson
notes.quote: This is I think the single worst spot on the schedule for any team this season.

notes.summary: Seattle's defensive strategy effectively eliminates the standard ground game but remains a major pass funnel for running backs out of the backfield.
notes.speaker: Brandon Anderson
notes.quote: They shut down the run game, they allowed the second fewest fantasy points to running backs, but the most running back receptions.

notes.summary: Daniels is expected back for Washington, but his health and rust levels are significant question marks on a highly congested injury report.
notes.speaker: Brandon Anderson
notes.quote: Washington has 23 names on their injury report.

notes.summary: Sean Payton has resumed playcalling duties, which is expected to result in a heavier rushing workload for the Broncos.
notes.speaker: Jo Madden
notes.quote: Sean Payton has taken back over the playcalling. I love that.

notes.summary: Chicago ranks 1st in the league in time of possession (36:35), whereas Green Bay ranks 31st (26:14). This limits Jordan Love's total pass attempts.
notes.speaker: Scott Bogman
notes.quote: Chicago has been hogging the ball; first in time of possession.

notes.summary: Arizona's struggling pass defense has allowed 11 passing touchdowns, presenting a strong matchup for Detroit pass catchers.
notes.speaker: Jo Madden
notes.quote: Arizona's pass defense has struggled, giving up 11 passing touchdowns.

notes.summary: Chris Brooks was sidelined for a third consecutive practice on Friday, cementing his expected absence for Week 5.
notes.speaker: Dave
notes.quote: Chris Brooks was out for the third straight day of practice today, Friday.

notes.summary: The league has not yet issued a ruling on Josh Jacobs, though Dave expects an eventual suspension of 6 to 8 games.
notes.speaker: Dave
notes.quote: I'm not sure what the NFL is waiting for here... I expected him to miss anywhere from six to eight games.

notes.summary: San Francisco's defensive front specializes in stopping zone runs, whereas Emanuel Wilson's effectiveness is limited when running gap schemes.
notes.speaker: Dave
notes.quote: The Seahawks do zone runs... San Francisco defends them well.

notes.topic: Rome Odunze usage vs Packers coverage
notes.summary: Green Bay's defensive tendency to drop into zone and generate minimal pressure allows Tyson Bagent extra time to target Odunze.
notes.speaker: Dave
notes.quote: The Packers have a zone leaning defense, they've got a low pass rush pressure rate.
